summary.text: Daughter of the master-thief Autolycus and mother of Jason by Aeson of Iolcus — in Apollodorus' genealogy the Argonaut inherits cunning from his mother's side as Odysseus does from the same grandfather.

story.text: Apollodorus names Polymede, daughter of Autolycus, as the woman by whom Aeson, son of Cretheus, begat Jason. The thief's line thus branches: Anticleia bore Odysseus to Laertes, and Polymede bore the man of the single sandal to Aeson — two heroes linked through the same grandfather's craft.
